{{recipe}} [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]]

This recipe for a sweetened '''potato pudding''' is from Cornwall, England.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) cooked [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]]
*1 stick (4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]/110 g) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]/½ [[Cookbook:Pint|pint]]) [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
*6 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*¾ cup ({{convert|6|oz|g|abbr=on|disp=s}}) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*¼ cup ({{convert|1|oz|g|abbr=on|disp=s}}) dried [[Cookbook:Currant|currants]]
*Zest of 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]
*½ whole [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]] kernel, grated
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Brandy|brandy]], or more to taste

==Procedure==
# Run the potatoes through a sieve, potato [[Cookbook:Ricer|ricer]], or mouli-mill.
# Gently heat butter and cream together until butter is melted. Mix into potatoes.
# Beat eggs lightly, then mix into potatoes. Mix in the sugar, currants, lemon zest, nutmeg, and brandy.
# Either transfer to pastry-lined [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|dish]] and bake in a moderately hot [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] until golden-brown OR [[Cookbook:Steaming|steam]] in a mould for about an hour.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*This recipe is dated to 1824 and is from ''St. Just W.I.'' in ''Cornish Recipes, Ancient & Modern, 22nd Edition'', The Cornwall Federation of Women's Institutes 1965. First collected & published by Edith Martin, Tregavethan, Truro, 1929, for The Cornwall F.of W. I.
